# YUGA — cannon carts and royal-chariot practice

The native Confluence arena is now 140 × 260 m with longer three-lane routes, eight landable decks, ten tether anchors and animated spear soldiers, bow guards and banner commanders. Paired waves fight, threaten cores and award once-only player last-hit gold. Reset starts a new local practice round. Cannon carts reinforce every third wave and royal chariots every fifth, subject to paired spawn clearance/capacity. Their committed ground blasts have visible anticipation and original sounds.

Extract the entire Linux or Windows ZIP. Run `launch.sh` or `launch.bat`, then choose **Explore Confluence**. Linux execution is reviewed separately from Windows archive validation. The default Forward+ renderer requires Vulkan; `--rendering-method gl_compatibility` is a reduced-effects fallback.

**Try the vehicles immediately:** Explore Confluence → Escape → Siege practice. F5 restores ordinary waves. The drill uses the same troop combat rules; siege blasts currently damage troops, not the hero.

Default controls: WASD move, mouse aim, left click bow, Space jump/rise, Ctrl descend, Shift sprint, Q pulse, E dash, R reload, F toggle flight, G tether/release, F1 overview, F2 help/remap, N daylight, Escape pause, F5 reset. Settings retain sound, sensitivity and custom bindings. Flight and tether need energy and a clear target.

The new `yuga-traversal-preview.mp4` contains six seconds of actual input-driven tether and flight capture at 1280 × 720, with five additional world/army stills. It is silent; its 30 FPS is simulated playback time from software rendering, not a hardware performance benchmark.

The separate `yuga-siege-preview.mp4` shows six seconds of continuous actual siege simulation after a single drill/camera setup. See `SIEGE-RENDER-REVIEW.md` for the reviewed frame limitations and `SIEGE-MILESTONE.md` for the roadmap.

The original music loop is included separately as `lane-procession-loop.wav`. Its synthesis, cue provenance and numerical tests are documented; human listening review is not claimed. `TRAVERSAL-VERIFICATION.md` identifies current evidence and practical limits.

This is offline native practice. Competitive native multiplayer, the full hero roster and production-quality character art remain open. The generated army/map concept is a future visual target. The separately included 24-second Confluence duel movie is unchanged archived cinematic work; it does not depict these new traversal mechanics.


Packages were rebuilt and checked at `35b20429d2b34f06f2907d5739cf4877aac597ab`. The MP4 and archived render reports retain their original captured source hashes; later tested playback fixes can differ from captured source. CI checks decoded media/audio correspondence and native headless scenarios; it does not rerender the film, listen to its sound, run Windows or measure hardware-GPU performance.

The separate yuga-traversal-preview.mp4 contains 180 consecutive rendered frames (six seconds at simulated 30 FPS). Its captured source inventory matches this checkout and the shared exported runtime sources. Five retained stills include separately staged city/army views. The traversal video is silent; real OS-input testing and hardware performance are separate evidence.
name: YUGA traversal and lane armies — native preview
